text:
maria: Ran the 10m burst repro against canary today, p95 barely moved but p99 jumped ~1.8x after scale-up. suspicion: kernel selector flips to the 'fast-bulk' path for medium batches which increases jitter on cold KV cache hits.

sam: hmm. did you capture the kernel selection log? can you paste the per-request metadata?

maria: pasted perf snippet below (super short):
```
[2026-07-22T14:03:01Z] req=ab12 kernel=fast-bulk batch=6 kv_hit=false seq_len=512 exec_ms=42
[2026-07-22T14:03:01Z] req=ab13 kernel=fast-bulk batch=1 kv_hit=false seq_len=32 exec_ms=290
[2026-07-22T14:03:02Z] req=ab14 kernel=fallback   batch=1 kv_hit=true  seq_len=32 exec_ms=18
```

maria: note the huge variance between the small single-item fast-bulk runs and the cached fallback. looks like fast-bulk path doesn't handle cold kv well; kernel choice multiplies cold penalty.

jordan: did we change the microbatch sizing heuristic recently? iirc we lowered the threshold to prefer fast-bulk at batch>=2.

maria: yeah, landed a tweak last month to reduce avg latency under steady-state. but during burst scale-up we see small batches + cold-kv mixing -> tails spike.

anna: ops perspective: autoscaler currently spins up N instances and routes immediately. we've got ~12s scale-up lag plus probe smoothing of 3s. if routing starts before KV prewarm completes, tails suffer.

sam: a few quick hypotheses: 1) kernel selector uses batch size + recent latency estimate but ignores per-instance KV-warmth. 2) microbatch sizing new rule biases towards smaller batches which triggers fast-bulk for many small requests. 3) prober samples insufficiently during burst so cache prewarm misses.

maria: i attached a small flamechart link (internal) and a p99 breakdown: cold-kv + kernel-switch = 60% of extra tail ms.

jordan: suggest two quick mitigations to test: a) add a short "cold grace" where newly started workers favor fallback kernel until they hit N cached prefixes, b) increase prober parallelism during scale-up to prewarm KV for common prefixes.

sam: agree. also we can bias microbatcher to wait up to X ms to form a size>1 batch during scale-up spikes; that reduces the number of single-item fast-bulk executions. maybe a dynamic microbatch window: if instance uptime < 20s, set max-wait=10ms.

maria: here's a proposed config snippet to try (toy):
```
{"kernel_warm_grace_s": 8, "prober_parallel": 4, "microbatch": {"base_wait_ms": 2, "cold_instance_wait_ms": 10}}
```

anna: can we also gate routing so newly-provisioned machines are not eligible for live traffic until prober reports >=80% common-prefix hit? that avoids immediate routing. may impact capacity though.

jordan: true, we'd need a fallback capacity pool to handle the ramp. or route to older nodes with slightly higher latency instead of cold new ones.

sam: for experiments, we should run a synthetic burst with mixed seq lengths: many short ones (16-64) + some long ones (512) to stress kernel heuristics. measure p95/p99 and log kernel path + kv_hit per request.

maria: i'll run AB test today on canary with the microbatch/kv-grace changes. will post results.

ci-bot: Deployment canary-2026-07-22T14:15 -> eng-runtime/canary started by maria. status: running probes.

maria: initial canary numbers after 5m: p95 ~ unchanged, p99 down ~25% vs baseline. early signs look promising. full run queued for 30m.

sam: awesome. once we validate, we should add a unit test for kernel_selector that includes a synthetic cold-kv signal (simulate kv_hit=false for first N requests) so we don't regress silently.

maria: noted. will open a follow-up PR with the test and the config toggle. thanks all :thumbsup:
